Having just come off of Ken Follett's The Pillars of the Earth, I told myself I needed a light-hearted experience. I realized very shortly that this...was not that. Story of a British soldier and a Shawnee girl as they travel together.

Kinetic novel, so no choices. No voices either. Writing is okay, not great but not terrible either. The setting seems interesting at first glance but they don't really do anything with it--you don't encounter civilization or really any of people acting out a "normal life." Art's okay, manages to feel moderately unique though I wouldn't call it super great. Music is alright, though I personally got a little tired of all the drum/marching/vaguely ominous pieces. Story is very short, but a rapport develops pretty organically between the soldier and the girl. Does an okay job of describing a character who really isn't a good guy but has good in him, which comes out around the girl. Not going to spoil the ending of course, but have to say that while overall the experience was definitely short, the ending was kind of fitting. All the plot threads were pretty properly tied off.

There are a couple things I found a little confusing: [spoiler]the dreams and Mai's final words. A pretty woman is entranced by a man, follows and lives with him, discovers that he's a "snake person," runs away from his snake form that chases her, is warned and led away by a bird spirit, returns to her old home to find it abandoned, stabs the snake with a spear, who turns back into the man, then she discovers her beauty is gone, and she then admonishes people she meets to look for beauty from within. I don't really see how this relates to the story, because the soldier is never shown to be looking for superficial beauty at all. And then Mai's last words--she calls the soldier her "brother." Incidentally, I just googled "Shawnee my brother" and the first link was to the "Shawnee Prophet" who was the brother of Tecumseh, who is mentioned in the VN, but apart from this I don't know of any specific reason why she calls him this.

In the end Aubrey asks Mai to wait for him in the sky, which makes me wonder if with all of this the devs were trying to intimate a romantic attraction. But that's only speculation; apart from that I don't understand these scenes.[/spoiler]

But all in all, it's a worthwhile experience on sale ($5 would be an appropriate regular price for this, not $9).

Over The Hills And Far Away is a short kinetic novel that takes place during 1812 where American and British soldiers fought in the Second War of Independence on American soil. The perspective follows William Aubrey, a redcoat that deserted the war effort after seeing his commander flee a battle where their forces were being overwhelmed. Later, as he is seeking shelter from a storm, he happens upon a lost Shawnee girl. This visual novel took me about three hours to read.

I enjoyed the game even though it was a bit short. The detailed backgrounds were beautiful, and I liked the character designs and concepts. The music was gorgeous, but not intrusive. However, there were a few (minor) issues I had with the game. It felt like some of the sound effects did not fit the action that was happening, which was a bit distracting. I also feel like the beginning portion was stretched a little too much; I think it overdid some of the interactions between the two main characters in the barn. It got to the point where it felt contrived and a bit unrealistic.

Overall, I enjoyed the visual novel and what it had to offer. For me, this feels like a one-and-done game. I don't regret buying the game, but it's not like the game especially amazed me. It wasn't great or bad. It's just a good game that can entertain you for a few hours. I would recommend giving this game a go on a sale if you are curious about it.

In summary this is basically a happy go lucky duo of adventurers. A soldier and a native 12yo girl. Sort of a Last of us/Telltale Walking dead sort of situation. You go to the native girls village, but in the end you get caught up by an officer and the little native girl gets shot as she tries to help you.

Conclusion: If it had more variety and more assets, and better pacing and some interactivity it would had been much better. As things stand you would be better off going to watch the movie Last of the Mohicans.

Over the Hills and Far Away is a kinetic novel set in one of the secondary theatres of the Napoleonic Wars, the American frontier, where British and Americans fought the Second War of Independence between 1812 and 1815, as a twin deterrent to the Peninsular War in Spain.
The game details a brief encounter far into the war in mid October 1813, and it offers a small perspecitve on the events of an unnamed battle badly lost by the British. The main character, Aubrey, is a British deserter who saw his commander flee the field of battle and his allies massacred. 

A little further into the novel the player realizes that the man is anything but good and, despite his attempts at redeeming himself, he is ultimately a bit of a scumbag. As it happens, he has an history with another man as bad as he was, and they have not settled the score yet. Moreover, he will soon find a cute little indian girl that happens to be lost in the storm.... yeah, If you thought "Oh my God this will be another of those wont it?" the answer is absolutely yes. Of course.
The story is not only short (under 5 hours) but incredibly stereotyped and telegraphed in its ending.
The most irritating thing about it is that all characters act like in a play, and not your regular western play, but a very Japanese animesque one. You basically have soldier-kun meets cute little indian-chan and the novel will make absolutely every effort to make you like her, to get you to see how cute and kind she is and how clumsy soldier-kun is. And you well know why, do you? Yes you do. Because the ending, the one. That one ending.

Visually speaking its nothing to write home about but it is absolutely decent for its price and effort put into it. It gets a full pass, I dont dislike it too much. The music is of course where all the budget went, good to great pieces of music, inspirational and put together nicely at the right moments.

All in all, this is - I'm not joking here, mind you - a copy-paste of Planetarian if the android girl was an indian in the flesh and the desperate post-apocalyptic protagonist was a Napoleonic soldier. There's even the exchange of the "memories" at the end. Almost word for word.

My advice here is, if you have already read Planetarian or one of the other million novels \ books about revenge with a girl in the middle used for "the one purpose", just skip this because you lose nothing. Buy the soundtrack instead which I believe has better value.
If you havent read other novels similar to this one, I would still tell you to skip it because there are better written ones, and more than anything else, far more respectful of the subject matter.

A lovely if sad story. I thouroughly enjoyed the setting and characters. A quick word of warning for some - there is no interaction in the story, so if this is a deal breaker you have been made aware.

A large amount of effort has been made to give the setting and different cultures an authenticity that most stories and visual novels flounder on. I was invested in the story throughout and thought that it gave a good impression of how tough and unforgiving America in this time period was. 

The characters are definitely multi-layered. Aubrey is certainly not a hero, however the game goes to great lengths to show you how he (and everyone else in the story) is a shade of grey rather than "good" and "bad". I felt that this certainly helped the story as it shows that everyone struggles with morality and made the characters far more believable.

Historically, the story is excellent. The language used and the attitudes displayed goes a long way for authenticity. It appears that research was done to do all cultures and environments justice, and to enhance this Aubrey unreliability as a narrator (and when his views are opposed) gives a fleshed out world.

The art and music is wonderful as well, and it is clear that this project was a labour of love for those that made it.

In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoyed the emotional rollercoaster I had over the two hours I read it. I was glad to support the studio and although their current production seems quite different, I hope they come back to doing something more like this in the future.

Despite my taste for reading, I've never been particularly drown to Visual Novels for a long time - probably because I didn't consider them exactly as games. Until one day I discovered [url=store.steampowered.com/app/446990/The_Huntsman_Winters_Curse/]The Huntsman : Winter's Curse[/url] : an excellent compromise between RPG and Visual Novel. It made me realize what a great adventure it can be : instead of staring at black on white books, you get to experience a story through not only text, but also pictures, musics, sounds, animations, sometimes even choices (note that it's not the case here); and that's what Over The Hills And Far Away has to offer : a marvelous and emotional tale to delight your mind, your eyes, your ears and your hearth.

I would definitely recommend Over The Hills And Far Away if you like Visual Novels, reading or great stories, especially if you can get it on sale. A longer story would have been nice, mostly because I'd like to know more about the Shawnee folklore. Also the last part feels a bit rushed and I was expecting more for this price. This is a lovely kinetic visual novel about a rogue redcoat making an unlikely friend in a young, Shawnee girl in the Michigan area during the War of 1812. It's a heartfelt slice of American historical fiction, and shows the cruelty of war for all involved, but particularly for Native Americans. 

Pros:
- Great writing
- Use of Shawnee language, culture, and folklore
- Emotionally charged ending
- Decent artwork
- A fair amount of humor

Cons:
- Too short (3 hours)

I definitely recommend it. It teaches the reader a little about the Shawnee people and elicits a sad realization of just how cruel white men were to Native Americans in those times.

A carefully written and well-written kinetic novel.  I want to emphasize that this is NOT a game per se, but rather a visual novel, a kind of illustrated story that progresses at the reader's pace.  Since it is a kinetic novel, I don't want to give spoilers in this review, but what I can say is that this novel is set during the War of 1812 in the Old Northwest, the region now comprising Michigan, Ohio, Indiana and Illinois.  The precise timeframe is not long after the Battle of the Thames, the battle that destroyed the British army in the western territories and secured the American hold on the original West of the country, laying the foundations for the full Westward expansion of the American people after the way.  It will be of interest to those who like history but don't know much about the history of the Old Northwest.  I think that it will be well-liked by anyone who likes carefully research and well-plotted historical fiction.  It is a bit short, but I think worth the purchase nonetheless.

This is a kinetic novel, so if you're expecting any gameplay or choice, look elsewhere. However, if you're willing to experience what is essentially a slideshow comic with a soundtrack, I can recommend this one. The art is very well done, though I wish there were more of it. There are 2 characters that really deserved having their own portraits since they're in more than one scene, but unfortunetly they just get text. A couple scenes reuse assets over again too much, and would have benefitted from some new art. Nevertheless, the story is quite different from most in this genre, and fairly touching too.

I wish I could give this game a neutral mark, but there isn't the option. There's good things in this game, but I'm not very happy that I've played it. 

Positives: The soundtrack is good ambient music, the credits vocal song and CG artwork are great, the conclusion was very emotional and touching. Including native American language deserves some credit,

Negatives: Having grown up reading Bernard Cornwall's Sharpe novels, and naturally associating the song 'Over the Hills and Far Away' with young British Tommys far from home, I was very disappointed that the protagonist has spent much of his life on the American frontier, losing the potential story of a stranger in a strange land. The story up to the conclusion wasn't the most original and left me emotionally cold, though I suppose the finale would've been spoilt if it hadn't got me a little. Without choices, or the advantages of movies, kinetic novels probably need to present threats and problems big and fast, and  the first 90% of this story didn't do that. Maybe the story from the vulnerable Mai's perspective would've grabbed me more.

[h1] Over The Hills And Far Away	[/h1]
A short visual novel that should be included in your history class. 

Playing as William Aubrey, a deserting soldier on the run; you hide in the barn for the harsh weather & execution order for deserting. 
However you find you're not alone, stuck with a Shawnee girl -May, who has too much backbone; you soon find yourself pulling out all your hair in frustration. 

This novel beautifuly displays the clash of cultures, and the awkward interaction between a harsh soldier & a young cunning girl.

[h1] Thumbs Up	[/h1]
The story is good, not totaly original - But far from cliché. 
Haven't seen a VN about the war in 1812 (or about war in general), Indians or their culture - However it heavily depends on an emotional build-up to the climax, which might not work for you. 

The graphic is beautiful - the backgrounds are truly well-made and a lot of details was put into every scene. Especially the facial expressions.

The music is a beautiful orchestrial masterpiece by Yuang Chen. I still listen to the soundtrack once in a while.

I found the text well-written. 
Now since May is a child, and Aubrey is not the most talkative person, the dialoque is rather simple, however that only shows their difference in persona, culture and objectives. 
Aubrey's lack of energy for dealing with May, and his self-pitying will make you laugh, hate and relate. 

[h1] Thumbs Down	[/h1]
Very short - 2-3 hours depending on your reading. 

It could include more history of May's background & culture. However Aubrey doesn't know much about it, and May doesn't tell much, so it'd feel out of place, if there were too much.  
Could be a DLC or extra feature for us who got interested. 

Some people miss branching paths.
- It would be nice with a longer story or alternative endings. [spoiler] Then we can cry more.	[/spoiler]

[h1] Closing Comments	[/h1]
A VN set in original settings, a little short but enjoyable all the way through. 
However like books; it's highly individual how you perceive the story, characters and philosophical aspects. 
Or if you want to re-read the story even while knowing the ending. 

The story has some similarities to Planetarian - the Reverie of a Little Planet-

What I like about this game is the developer tend to stay away from cliche setting we often see in any other visual novels; highschool teens drama, instead it happens during the War of 1812 (a conflict between United States & British Empire), where the story focus on a British deserter & a young Indian girl.

While the story may be slow & lack of engaging dialogue for some players, the interaction between a rude & harsh soldier and a young but cunning Indian girl is well portrayed by how awkward but entertaining it can be. CG artworks are beautiful, but since the game is short, not so many places can be covered, which I find it disappointing. Among them, there is a villain character from different faction, which is well-portrayed based on his malice & grudge, enough to make me feel like punching him in the face.

For a short kinetic novel like this, I suggest you to buy this during sale.

Also, be prepared for whats coming, for you may not like where the story is leading.

Ich finde auch, die beiden Charaktere sind aus psychologischer Sicht ganz gut getroffen: Der desillusionierte, abgebrühte, ans Töten gewöhnte Krieger, der sich dagegen sträubt, Gefühle zuzulassen, aber dann ahnen lässt, dass doch noch ein Rest Menschlichkeit übriggeblieben ist....
Das anfangs naiv und fast dümmlich wirkende, aber im Grunde ziemlich schlaue Indianermädchen - es ist schon eine eigenartige, aber eigentlich nicht unglaubwürdige Beziehung zwischen den Beiden (vor allem wenn man das alles in dem historischen Kontext betrachtet).

Kann sein, dass nach etwas zähem Beginn zum Schluss hin das Emotionale etwas überzeichnet wirken kann, aber ich denke, die Entwickler haben es schon richtig gemacht, zu zeigen, dass es im Krieg sehr oft die Schwächsten (die Kinder) sind, die es am härtesten trifft!

Over the Hills and Far Away has been on my wishlist for quite some time now and I finally bought it months ago and I don't regret it.

Pros

- Takes place during a historical period that most people don't care to remember. I searched about it and it's actually a lot more important than people think it is and it's worth reading about.

- The artwork is fantastic. Filled with personality, the details are delicate but rough in the right places and very pleasing to the eyes.

- Since it's a kinetic novel, you can sit back and watch it like a movie with subtitles.

- Story wise, it isn't the most original out there but it's bittersweet and I almost cried. The prose is great.

- The music is also beautiful. I wouldn't mind having the OST. It's orchestra, no synths, which it may not be historically accurate? But it fits.

- The devs also did their research, I absolutely loved how Mai spoke her language, you rarely see Native Americans represented in media and I'm happy to see so much effort in building Mai.

Cons

- Some people may not like that's it a kinetic novel.

- Some may find it too short.

- Some people may hate the tragic theme, especially since it's kind of easy to assume that it will happen.

I love stories with bittersweet endings. What I love even more than that is when stories are well put together, well writen, and keep my attention til the very end which this VN did. Definitely worth the money I spent. Thank you for making this!

I see many reviewers saying this is set during the American War for Independence - that's not correct.  The story is set during the War of 1812, sometimes called the Second War of Independence.  Aubrey says "this is the 1800s" as part of his dialog.  Also, he refers to Chief Tecumseh being killed.  Tecumseh was killed at the Battle of the Thames in October 1813.

Highly recommended VN.
